title: FloodGuard Refund Interest Day Count
content:
**Training note — interest days on FloodGuard Private Flood Policy refunds**

Refund interest days are counted as follows: when the cancellation date precedes the date the cancellation request was received, as recorded on the request whether or not it had been signed by then, and the customer's HomeGuard Homeowners Policy at the same property address ended within 7 days of the cancellation date, from the date the request was received to the refund date; when the cancellation date precedes the date the request was received without that corroboration, no interest days are counted; and otherwise from the cancellation date to the refund date.

**Questions answered**

*Which cancellation date is meant?* The date the flood policy's coverage ended, as shown on the cancelled policy.

*When does a HomeGuard policy corroborate?* When the customer's HomeGuard Homeowners Policy at the same property address as the flood policy ended no more than 7 calendar days before or after the cancellation date. An ending 7 days away corroborates; one 8 days away does not; a HomeGuard policy at that address that has not ended does not.

*What if the cancellation date is the same day as, or later than, the date the request was received?* The cancellation date does not precede it, so the days run from the cancellation date to the refund date, whatever the HomeGuard policy shows.

**Hypothetical calendar.** Cancellation date 1 March; request received 11 March, as recorded on the request; refund issued 20 April.

| HomeGuard at the same address | Interest days |
|---|---|
| Ended 4 March | 40 (11 March to 20 April) |
| Ended 20 March | none |
| Still in force | none |

Had the request been received on 1 March itself, the interest days would be 50 (1 March to 20 April), whatever the HomeGuard policy shows.
